report:
I graded all 47 windows and the shard holds all 47 (0 rejects after one fix). Grades: 21 × 2, 9 × 1, 17 × 0, no −1.

The final `label get judgment --intent test_speedup_after_person` crashes before listing anything. Another intent's window, `l1x_dream_recover_person_present|GDC_Library_42:0297`, appears in two shards (`ep-l1x_dream_recover_person_present.jsonl` and `ex-l1x_dream_recover_person_present-j1.jsonl`), so the store refuses to load. Adding a shard priority in `labels/precedence.json` would fix it; I didn't touch that. I checked `annotations/labels/judgment/l2-test_speedup_after_person-v9-p1.jsonl` directly instead. Grade 0 isn't written to the file, so the zeros show up only as lines with no grade.

I read the intent as its oracle in `compose_test.json` defines it: a person appears ahead, then a speed-up of at least 0.3 m/s starts within 3 s. The speed-up start is the anchor, with 4 s of context either side.

**Episodes** (speeds are the smoothed values from `signals`):

| Recording | Speed-up start | Speed | Person evidence | Qualifies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bass_Garage_134 | 7.3, 9.9, 12.7 s | +0.40, +0.64, +0.45 m/s | dense crowd; new walkers enter the front body cameras (frontleft #42, #50) | yes |
| Bass_Garage_134 | 29.5 s | 0.96→1.27 m/s in exactly 2.0 s, just over the bar | walkers close in front (#126) | yes |
| Bass_Garage_134 | 56.6 s | 0.94→1.49 m/s | people crossing ahead (#247) | yes |
| Bass_Garage_134 | 83.4 s | 0.69→1.37 m/s | at the foot of stairs; only distant figures (>20 m) come into view (#370) | partial |
| Bass_Garage_134 | 91.0–91.4 s | 0.68→1.39 m/s | group ~10–15 m ahead appears as the robot levels off the stairs (#405) | yes |
| Brackenridge | 52.8 s | 1.46→1.99 m/s | the pair it passes had been visible since ~47 s | no |
| Brackenridge | 64.8 s | 1.52→1.96 m/s | distant people come into view on a right turn | weak |
| Butler | 62.0 s | 1.02→1.40 m/s in 1.9 s | new pair close on the left in a tailgate crowd (#1784) | yes |
| GDC_Library_42 | 299.5 s | 0.88→1.46 m/s | new pedestrians enter the path (#8913) | yes |
| JCL | 5.7 s | 0.70→1.13 m/s | new person close on the right (#74) | yes |
| JCL | 62.8 s | 0.30→0.84 m/s | people come into view while turning (#1813) | yes |
| Library_Jester_75 | 43.6 s | 0.69→1.05 m/s | man appears at the doorway at 42.0 s (#1215) | yes |
| Library_Jester_75 | 48.1 s | 0.24→0.86 m/s | people in the hallway | yes |
| Library_MLK | ~26 s, from a standstill | to 0.53 m/s within 2 s | people visible through the opened door (#690) | yes |
| Library_MLK | 37.0 s | 0.99→1.49 m/s | new pedestrians ahead (#996) | yes |
| Library_MLK | 73.5 s | 0.91→1.25 m/s | person coming down the stairs ahead (#2124) | yes |

GDC, Library_Fountain_5 (steady 1.88–2.02 m/s) and the Butler 47/80 and Jester 64 windows have no speed-up, so they're all 0. Bass_Garage 34.5–36 s is a near-miss at +0.24 m/s, so window 39 is 0.

**What the data can't settle** (for `answered_partial`):
- **"New person" in dense crowds.** In Bass_Garage 5–60 s and Butler someone new enters the view every second or two, so the person condition holds trivially. The data can't show that the speed-up had anything to do with a person.
- **"Appears" after stairs or turns.** People often "appear" only because the camera levels off after stairs or the robot turns. I counted that when people were within about 15 m, and graded it partial when they were only far-off figures (Bass_Garage 83.4 s, Brackenridge 64.8 s).
- **Anchor timing.** The smoothed speed lags by about 0.45 s, so a few windows sit right at the 1 s edge: Bass_Garage 29, 34 and 96, and Jester 48. I used the raw speed minimum to decide them, and they all came out as 2.
- **Bass_Garage_134 has no forward payload camera.** Person evidence there comes from the frontleft/frontright body cameras, whose images arrive about 0.2–0.45 s after capture.
